site.name: Black Prince Mine
site.location: Black Tiger Gulch / Boulder County tungsten district
overview: Black Prince Mine is a documented historic mine in Black Tiger Gulch within Boulder County's tungsten district, where federal geological work recorded several underground tunnels on the southwest side of the gulch.

timeline.text: Black Prince was developed as a group of underground workings in Black Tiger Gulch during the district's tungsten-mining period.
U.S. Geological Survey Professional Paper 245 documented four Black Prince tunnels and their relationship to the geology of the Boulder County tungsten district.

moreHistory: USGS Professional Paper 245 places four Black Prince tunnels at approximately 6,725, 6,870, 6,955, and 7,000 feet elevation on the southwest side of Black Tiger Gulch, about 1,500 feet from its mouth, and includes a geologic plan of the workings.

sourceReferences.title: Geology and ore deposits of the Boulder County tungsten district, Colorado — Professional Paper 245
sourceReferences.note: Documents the Black Prince tunnels in Black Tiger Gulch and provides component-level mine geometry.
